Base Imagery.name: True Color
Base Imagery.subtitle: Current (VIIRS NOAA-21)
Base Imagery.description: Default base map. Most current-generation daily true color, 375m. Use for 'what does it look like today/recently'.

Base Imagery.name: True Color — Long Record (MODIS Terra)
Base Imagery.description: Only true-color option with a record back to 2000. Use for multi-year/decade before-after comparisons, not day-to-day snapshots.

Base Imagery.name: Blue Marble — Static Reference
Base Imagery.description: Static NASA Blue Marble reference imagery. Good fallback base when daily imagery is patchy; loads at Level8.

Precipitation.name: Rainfall — Right Now (IMERG NRT)
Precipitation.description: Near-real-time global precipitation, 10km, updated every 30 min. The 'is it raining there today' layer. Use dates within the last few days.

Precipitation.name: Rainfall — Historical Event (IMERG Archive)
Precipitation.description: IMERG archive for reconstructing a specific past storm. Needs a full ISO datetime. Example default set to Cyclone Freddy's Mozambique landfall.

Vegetation.name: Vegetation Health — Trend (NDVI Monthly)
Vegetation.description: Monthly NDVI composite, least cloud noise. Use for season-to-season or year-to-year comparison stories (crop stress, greening/browning trends).

Vegetation.name: Vegetation Health — Current (NDVI 8-Day)
Vegetation.description: Current-generation 8-day NDVI composite. Use when the monthly layer is too stale for a fast-moving story.

Air Quality.name: Air Pollution — NO2 (TROPOMI)
Air Quality.description: Best-available NO2 column, ~7km, near-daily. Urban pollution, industrial emissions, biomass burning. Use for city air-quality stories.

Air Quality.name: Dust & Smoke — Aerosols (MODIS AOD)
Air Quality.description: Combined aerosol optical depth, 10km. The Saharan dust / biomass-burning-smoke layer. Central for the Southern Africa burning-season and Sahara dust stories.

Air Quality.name: Volcanic/Industrial — SO2 (TROPOMI)
Air Quality.description: SO2 vertical column, ~7km, near-daily. Detects volcanic eruptions and industrial/power-plant emissions. Kept specifically for East African Rift volcano stories (e.g. Nyiragongo).

Wildfire.name: Active Fires — Now (VIIRS NOAA-20)
Wildfire.description: Flagship active-fire point layer, 375m, day+night. This is the headline wildfire layer.

Wildfire.name: Active Fires — Now (VIIRS NOAA-21, extra pass)
Wildfire.description: Same product family as NOAA-20, adds an extra daily overpass. Surface as a togglable variant under 'Active Fires', not a separate menu item.

Wildfire.name: Active Fires — Now (VIIRS SNPP, extra pass)
Wildfire.description: Same product family, oldest VIIRS platform. Togglable variant under 'Active Fires' for maximum daily coverage.

Wildfire.name: Active Fires — Historical Record (MODIS)
Wildfire.description: Coarser (1km) but the only fire-detection layer with a record back to the early 2000s. Use for 'is this worse than previous years' comparison stories.

Wildfire.name: Burn Scars — False Color (VIIRS)
Wildfire.description: 375m false color; burn scars appear orange-red. Use alongside the active-fire points to show cumulative damage, not just today's detections.

Floods.name: Flood Extent — Now (VIIRS, 375m)
Floods.description: Best-resolution near-real-time flood extent. A frequent, distinct African story from precipitation — this is the 'impact' layer, IMERG is the 'cause' layer.

Drought.name: Soil Moisture — Surface (SMAP L3)
Drought.description: Surface (0-5cm) soil moisture, ~36km, daily. Responds fast to rainfall deficit — use this over the L4 root-zone product for single-season drought stories.

Drought.name: Land Surface Temperature — Day (MODIS)
Drought.description: 1km daily daytime land surface temp. The heat-stress companion to soil moisture.

Drought.name: Groundwater Anomaly (GRACE-FO)
Drought.description: ~300km, monthly. Coarse, but the only satellite product that sees deep aquifer depletion. Kept specifically for basin-scale stories: Lake Chad, Nile/GERD.

Context.name: Population Density (GPW v4)
Context.description: ~5km. Not a story on its own — an overlay to turn any hazard layer into 'who is affected'. Offer as a toggle across all story modes, not its own category.

Overlays.name: Coastlines
Overlays.description: Static vector coastline reference overlay. Uses the GIBS 'default' time keyword, so it is date-independent and always available.

Overlays.name: Place Labels
Overlays.description: Place and country labels (GIBS Reference_Labels, Level9). Static reference overlay.

Overlays.name: Reference Features
Overlays.description: Political border and feature lines (GIBS Reference_Features, Level9). Static reference overlay.

Overlays.name: Graticule Grid
Overlays.description: Latitude/longitude graticule (GIBS Graticule_15m, Level13). Static reference overlay.

Overlays.name: Land Mask
Overlays.description: OpenStreetMap-derived land/ocean mask (GIBS OSM_Land_Mask, Level9). Darkens oceans as an underlay.

_notes.provenance: Trimmed from the original ~150-layer catalogue (validated HTTP 200 against GIBS June 2026) down to 19 layers across 6 story categories + base imagery + one context overlay. Layer metadata (tileMatrixSet, format, legendId) copied as-is from that validated file — re-verify endpoints before shipping, since this pass only selected and re-tagged entries, it didn't re-hit the GIBS endpoint.
_notes.storyFirstUI: Each category has one or more 'role: primary, storyDefault: true' layers meant to load automatically when a user picks that story mode. 'secondary' and 'context' layers are opt-in toggles, not separate top-level menu items.
_notes.fireGrouping: The three VIIRS active-fire layers share group: 'active_fires_viirs' — render as one feature with a satellite-pass toggle, not three menu entries.
_notes.compositeDates: NDVI monthly/8-day products use period-boundary dates — changing arbitrarily will 404.
_notes.timeFormat: Per-layer dates are intentionally NOT stored here — resolved at runtime (default for daily layers is yesterday). Most layers use YYYY-MM-DD. IMERG archive uses full ISO datetime.
_notes.graceLag: GRACE-FO has a historically multi-month to multi-year processing/release lag — when loading it, pick a date at least several months old.
_notes.geoSatellites: GIBS has no useful geostationary coverage over Africa (its GEO layers are GOES/US-centric; Meteosat, which covers Africa, is EUMETSAT-only and not in GIBS). IMERG already fuses GEO-IR data internally, so this gap doesn't block the precipitation story.
